variants.descriptor: The vessel is shown in its Block-II mid-life refit configuration, with additional bolted-on armor panels along the flanks, an upgraded sensor mast, and clearly visible modernization seams between the original and refit panel courses.

The vessel is shown in a civilian conversion: turrets removed or faired over with smooth panel covers, additional cargo blisters and viewport rows added along the flanks, and a civilian livery panel layout replacing the original military markings.

The vessel is shown in a pirate conversion: mismatched salvaged armor patches over the hull, jury-rigged extra weapon mounts welded onto the dorsal spine, asymmetric bolt-on hull modifications and exposed bundled cabling running along the flanks.

The vessel is shown in a stealth configuration: flush faceted radar-absorbent paneling replacing the standard armor courses, recessed vents flush with the hull, no protruding antennas, and minimal external greebles, giving the silhouette a smoother and more angular read while keeping the same overall proportions.

The vessel is shown as a prototype trial unit: exposed test instrumentation harnesses running along the flanks, unpainted primer-grey panels alongside finished sections, hand-stenciled trial unit markings on the bow, and visible experimental sensor pods bolted to non-standard locations.

The vessel is shown in ceremonial flagship livery: ornate dress paneling and gilded trim along the armor belt, an oversized fleet command antenna mast, ceremonial banners or insignia plates affixed to the dorsal hull, and a polished parade-ground finish on all visible surfaces.

The vessel is shown heavily battle-damaged: torn armor plating with jagged edges, exposed internal frame structure in the damaged sections, scorched and blackened paint around impact zones, missing turrets or antenna stubs, and makeshift welded patch repairs over hull breaches.

The vessel is shown in veteran ace markings: a distinctive personal paint scheme replacing standard fleet livery, a row of small painted kill-marks stenciled across the flank near the bridge, a custom hand-painted unit emblem on the bow, and one or two oversized stylized accent stripes wrapping the hull, giving the impression of a lived-in personal hero ship.

The vessel is shown as a captured hull repurposed by a different faction: the original livery is partially overpainted with mismatched new colors, original markings are visible faintly bleeding through under the new paint, replacement antennas and weapon mounts of a clearly different manufacturing style are bolted on at non-original positions, and welded patch plates cover original panel cutouts.
